description: issue #682 (slice I3): registration is not invocation, and `"stop"` is a REQUESTED stop notification — a headless batch `execute()` run receives no such request, so a `when "stop" [ ... ]` handler is registered (emitting the `instruction`+`primitive` pair, seq 0-1) but never fires. Unlike `"start"` (already being delivered because the run has started), `"stop"` is not delivered here; the following `print "mid"` runs (seq 2-3) and that is the whole event stream — `"bye"` is never printed. This slice deliberately does NOT synthesize a `"stop"` event on natural completion, which spec/interaction-events.md (§`### when <event-word> <block>`, "stop for a requested stop notification before termination") does not define as a stop request. Description reconciled by #688 (terminal slice): delivering `"stop"` no longer belongs to a later host slice — #686/I7's `ExecuteOptions.hostInput` can schedule ANY named event, `"stop"` included, and doing so does fire this handler. What this fixture pins is therefore narrower and still exactly true: reaching the end of a batch run is not itself a stop REQUEST, so with no host input scheduling one, `"stop"` is never delivered.
